UTC: Coordinated Universal Time. The primary time standard used in aviation worldwide; all aviation weather reports, flight plans, and NOTAMs reference UTC to ensure a consistent global time reference.
VA: Volcanic ash. Airborne fine particles of pulverised rock and glass ejected during volcanic eruptions; a significant aviation hazard that can cause engine failure, abrasion, and navigation system damage.
VAAC: Volcanic Ash Advisory Centre. A specialised meteorological centre responsible for monitoring volcanic ash clouds and issuing advisories to aviation, coordinated through nine regional centres worldwide under ICAO.
VAL: In valleys. A location qualifier used in NOTAM text and weather reports indicating that a phenomenon or condition is occurring within valley terrain, which may affect local wind patterns and visibility.
VAN: Runway control van. A mobile or fixed facility at an aerodrome from which air traffic services or ground movement control of the runway area is exercised, typically equipped with communication and surveillance equipment.
VAR: Magnetic variation. The angular difference between true north and magnetic north at a given location, expressed in degrees east or west; essential for converting between true and magnetic headings in navigation.
VCY: Vicinity. A proximity qualifier used in NOTAM text and meteorological reports indicating that a condition or phenomenon is occurring near (typically within 8 to 16 km of) the aerodrome reference point.
VER: Vertical. Relating to the up-down axis or elevation; used in NOTAM text to describe the vertical extent or dimension of airspace, obstacles, or weather phenomena.
VI: Heading to an intercept. A flight navigation instruction indicating that the aircraft is to maintain a heading to intercept a specific track, radial, or course, typically used in radar vectoring or instrument approach procedures.
VIP: Very important person. A status designation used in NOTAM text and airport operations to indicate flights or movements involving persons of high priority, requiring special handling, security, or ground services.
VIS: Visibility. The greatest distance at which prominent objects can be seen and identified under daylight conditions; a critical meteorological parameter reported in METAR, TAF, and NOTAM for flight operations.
VLR: Very long range. A classification indicating extended operational range capability for aircraft, navigation aids, or communication systems, typically exceeding standard range parameters.
VMC: Visual meteorological conditions. Meteorological conditions expressed in terms of visibility, distance from cloud, and ceiling equal to or better than specified minima, allowing VFR flight operations.
VORTAC: VOR and TACAN combination. A combined navigational aid providing both VOR azimuth guidance and TACAN distance measuring and bearing information at a single facility, enabling both civil and military aircraft navigation.
VPA: Vertical path angle. The angle of the vertical flight path relative to the horizontal plane, typically expressed in degrees; used in approach procedure design and performance calculations.
VRB: Variable. A qualifier used in aviation weather reports and NOTAMs to indicate that wind direction, visibility, or other parameters are changing significantly and cannot be reported as a steady value.
VSP: Vertical speed. The rate of ascent or descent of an aircraft, typically expressed in feet per minute (ft/min) or metres per second (m/s); critical for flight path management and instrument approaches.
VTF: Vector to final. An ATC radar procedure in which an IFR aircraft is vectored onto the final approach course to intercept the localiser or final approach path, bypassing intermediate approach segments.
WAAS: Wide Area Augmentation System. A satellite-based augmentation system (SBAS) developed by the FAA that improves GPS accuracy, integrity, and availability for aviation navigation, enabling precision approaches down to Category I.
WAFC: World Area Forecast Centre. One of two ICAO-designated centres (London and Washington) that prepare and disseminate global forecasts of upper winds, temperatures, and significant weather phenomena for international aviation.
WB: Westbound. A direction qualifier indicating flight or movement in a westerly direction, used in NOTAM text, route descriptions, and flow management to specify direction of travel.
WBAR: Wing bar lights. A series of lights installed on the wing tips or along the wing of an aircraft or on the ground at an aerodrome to indicate aircraft position, or as part of the approach lighting system.
WDI: Wind direction indicator. A ground-based device at an aerodrome that shows the direction of the surface wind, such as a windsock, wind tee, or tetrahedron; essential for pilot situational awareness during take-off and landing.
WDSPR: Widespread. A qualifier in NOTAM text and weather reports indicating that a phenomenon or condition affects a large geographic area rather than being localised.
WED: Wednesday. A day-of-week abbreviation used in NOTAM text and aviation scheduling to specify the day an event, operation, or condition is effective.
WGS-84: World Geodetic System 1984. The standard geodetic reference system used in aviation for positioning, navigation, and charting; all ICAO standard coordinates for waypoints, navaids, and aerodromes are expressed in WGS-84.
WI: Within. A spatial qualifier in NOTAM text indicating a condition or phenomenon occurring inside a specified distance or area boundary from a reference point.
WID: Width or wide. A dimension qualifier used in NOTAM text and aerodrome documentation to specify the lateral extent of a runway, taxiway, obstacle, or restricted area.
WILCO: Will comply. A radiotelephony acknowledgement phrase indicating that the received instruction has been understood and will be carried out by the receiving aircraft or station.
WIP: Work in progress. A NOTAM qualifier indicating that construction, maintenance, or repair activities are being conducted on or near the movement area of an aerodrome, posing potential hazards to aircraft.
WKN: Weaken or weakening. A trend descriptor in aviation weather reports and forecasts indicating that a weather phenomenon (such as a thunderstorm, tropical cyclone, or frontal system) is decreasing in intensity.
WNW: West north west. An intercardinal compass direction (bearing 292.5 degrees) used in navigation, weather reports, and NOTAM text to indicate direction relative to true or magnetic north.
WO: Without. A qualifier used in NOTAM text and aviation documentation to indicate the absence of a specified feature, equipment, condition, or service.
WPT: Waypoint. A defined geographical position used for navigation, specified by coordinates (latitude/longitude) and typically associated with RNAV procedures; waypoints are used to define routes, approaches, and airspace boundaries.
WRNG: Warning. A notification in NOTAM text and aviation safety communications alerting pilots, ATC, or ground personnel to actual or potential hazards affecting flight safety or aerodrome operations.
WS: Wind shear. A sudden change in wind speed and/or direction over a short distance, either vertically or horizontally; a significant aviation hazard, particularly during take-off, approach, and landing phases.
WSPD: Wind speed. The rate of air movement measured in knots (kt) or metres per second (m/s), reported in METAR, TAF, and NOTAM text; a fundamental parameter for flight planning and aircraft performance calculations.
WSW: West south west. An intercardinal compass direction (bearing 247.5 degrees) used in navigation, weather reports, and NOTAM text to indicate direction relative to true or magnetic north.
WT: Weight. The mass of an aircraft, cargo, or object expressed in kilograms or pounds; used in performance calculations, load planning, and NOTAMs for weight-restricted operations.
WTSPT: Waterspout. An intense columnar vortex of air over water, often associated with cumuliform clouds; a significant aviation hazard that may be reported via SIGMET or NOTAM when observed near flight routes.
WWW: World Wide Web. The global system of interconnected hypertext documents accessed via the internet; used in aviation as a reference to online publications, NOTAM distribution systems, and web-based flight planning tools.
WX: Weather. A general abbreviation used in NOTAM text, flight documentation, and aviation communications to refer to current or forecast meteorological conditions affecting flight operations.
WXR: Weather radar. An airborne or ground-based radar system used to detect and display precipitation, turbulence, and wind shear; essential for weather avoidance and situational awareness during flight.
XNG: Crossing. A navigation term indicating that an aircraft is crossing a waypoint, fix, boundary, or another aircraft's path; used in ATC communications and NOTAM text to describe route intersections.
XS: Atmospherics. Natural electromagnetic disturbances in the radio frequency spectrum, typically caused by lightning discharges; may affect radio communications and navigation signal reception.
YR: Your. A possessive pronoun used in NOTAM text and ATC communications to indicate association with the addressee or the aircraft being addressed.
AC: Altocumulus. A mid-level cloud type (ICAO classification) composed of white or grey patches, layers, or sheets of rounded masses; often indicates instability aloft and may precede thunderstorms.
ACTIVE: Active. A status indicator used in the FAA Pilot/Controller Glossary to describe a runway, airspace, or facility that is currently in operational use and available for aircraft operations.
ACTUAL: Actual. A term used in the FAA Pilot/Controller Glossary to refer to the calculated landing time based on real-time operational data, as opposed to scheduled or estimated times.
ADVISORY: Advisory service. An FAA Pilot/Controller Glossary term for a service provided by air traffic control that offers advice and information to pilots to assist in the safe conduct of flight, including traffic advisories and weather information.
